Critics Consensus Powerfully moving and emotionally resonant, Wild finds director Jean-Marc Vallée and star Reese Witherspoon working at the peak of their respective powers. Read Critics Reviews Candice Frederick Reel Talk Online 09/01/2017 But despite its unclear message, there is a certain charm to Wild that smooths away its thorny exterior to reveal a broken character... Go to Full Review Jason Bailey Flavorwire 06/07/2016 For all of the trouble 'Wild' takes to get into Strayed's head, you'd think they might've drafted filmmakers with a little bit more experience living in a place like that. Go to Full Review David Sims The Atlantic 10/14/2015 It captures an emotional memoir without making it feel like a didactic tale of triumph over adversity. Go to Full Review Sean Axmaker Stream on Demand 11/16/2024 While there is a conventional backbone to the story, it keeps us rooted in the experience of a single woman taking on a challenge that some veteran hikers fail to complete, never forgetting the vulnerability of doing it alone. Go to Full Review Benjamín Harguindey EscribiendoCine 01/17/2024 As usual, Witherspoon is fearless, headstrong, and tireless. [Full review in Spanish] Go to Full Review Brian Eggert Deep Focus Review 07/13/2022 Witherspoon's performance is outstanding. Go to Full Review Read all reviews Stella B @RT93004439 Apr 1 Extrimely slow and boring Sabrina C @SabrinaCheek Jan 17 Reese Witherspoon's work here was both passionate and dedicated. She clearly had great respect for her source material, and did it justice. The film was a sincere reflection on grief, addiction, divorce, and the hustle and bustle of modern life. It is an important reminder to take moments to breathe, and shines love for nature even when it hurts. See more Natasha R @MsNatasha Jan 5 I read this book a few years back - this movie matched up pretty well to my memory of the book. I found myself wondering what exactly might lead someone to do the PCT on their own with minimal training and/or experience. I know that she had a lot of help on the trail and that in all honesty was a burden to others (according to some stories that came out after all of this). But logistics aside, this is a great story. It takes a lot of courage to do something this difficult, and it is pretty inspiring to do it alone. View More Most Inspiring Movies Most Inspiring Movies 24:28 View more videos Synopsis Driven to the edge by the loss of her beloved mother (Laura Dern), the dissolution of her marriage and a headlong dive into self-destructive behavior, Cheryl Strayed (Reese Witherspoon) makes a decision to halt her downward spiral and put her life back together again. With no outdoors experience, a heavy backpack and little else to go on but her own will, Cheryl sets out alone to hike the Pacific Crest Trail -- one of the country's longest and toughest through-trails.
